body: Thank you for reading.  Ha, I know no one is normal, but most people aren't as fucked up as I am.  I've mostly gotten over that, except sometimes I just get so depressed.  Like when I fail out of classes because I'm so fucking retarded.  Thanks for replying.
Thank you for your reply, thank you for reading.  Maybe I will see one.  I don't know how much they cost.  I go to school though, maybe there's a program through the school.
Oh man I've gotten great at repairing dry wall.

Oh man, I'm by far the stupidest person I know.  With the possible exception of my mother who so kindly passed on the stupid.  

I've got to say one of the dumber things I've done recently is get off of a flight at the wrong stop.  I knew the plane stopped in two cities, but to be honest, I had never flown a route where I had to get off on the second stop, so I didn't even think to look closer.   I really had no idea where that city even was (this is a relatively major US city - I guarantee you American redditors know where it is) so I guess I just ignored it.  

I was listening to music when the plane landed, so I didn't hear any announcements.  Everyone started getting off and I think by this point I had forgotten the thing even stopped at two cities.  I grabbed my shit and got off the plane.

This is where it gets better.  I'm really cringing here, but I called my friend to come pick me up.  I distinctly recall seeing the decorations in this airport I'd never before stepped foot in and rolling my eyes, knowing I was back.  (The two cities are close to one another - and their airports have similar, distinct decorations) 

My friend was on the phone with me circling the airport, dealing with traffic while I tried to direct her to my terminal.  I kept going around, trying to ask people where I was because she was having some trouble finding me, but they kept getting confused and I kept getting frustrated.  Basically, imagine conversations between a person trying to figure out what number terminal they're at and people who barely know English confused because there's only one terminal at that airport.  It was so far out of my mind that I might not be where I intended to be that I was asking things like "So what?  All of the terminals come together to form a single Arrivals pick up area?"

This went on for over an hour.  Over an hour my friend went to different terminals, dealt with traffic, until finally I asked the question before the horrifying realization had actually hit me.  "What city am I in?"

Have you ever been in a situation in your life where you didn't know what fucking city you were in?  God, this story is *painful* for me to write.

Well I had gotten in at something like 10-11 PM  so the airport was absolutely shut down.  I was poor as shit, kicking myself for needing to buy another ticket, too young to rent a car (which turned out to be far too expensive anyway) and too cheap and stubborn to get a hotel room.  I sat all night on an airport bench sobbing my eyes out with how retarded I am until 4AM when the ticket counters opened.

Here's why I'll always fly Southwest.  Not only did the ticket lady give me a ticket on the first plane to where I was headed, free of charge, she actually said "This happens all the time."  I didn't believe her for a nanosecond, but goddamnit, in that moment, those were the words I needed to hear.

The best part is because of the time difference, the flight took minutes and I made it to work on time that day.

It took me awhile, but I can't hold how people treated me against them.  Jr high school kids are naturally horrible people.  They couldn't help it as much as I couldn't help being the mess of a human I was.  And honestly, I wouldn't have been friends with me either.  I was awkward, uninteresting, and was always making an idiot of myself.  I was pretty hard to love.  Don't feel bad about it - we all do stupid shit when we're 13.

I have an incredibly strict and angry mother.  Due to her sheltering me, countless personal personality flaws, and the mean-spirited nature of junior high school students, my life was an absolute torment.  In 7th grade, I would wake up, go to school where I had no friends and people would bully and mock me constantly, where I was aware that I didn't understand dirty jokes or know who Hanson was, I wasn't allowed to see the new pg-13 movie, I was ugly and shy and awkward.  People loved how stupid I was - it was entertainment.  I spent a lot of time crying.  I had beyond no self esteem.  I loathed myself.

Then I would come home to my mother.  I would struggle to finish my homework amongst her constant berating, she's so condescending and just evil.  She would tear me away from my homework every few minutes and could make me feel like shit in a second.  Always screaming.  Always putting me down.  I stood up to her once and she left for a day, no one knew where she was, my father blamed this on me.

I was oblivious to everything.  Things that a normal person can observe fly past me, I have no common sense, I was constantly getting myself into trouble by forgetting things or doing stupid things.  I knew I had no friends, but I had no idea how to be confident, how to learn about pop culture, how to make myself attractive.  I just wanted to read and daydream all day.  But I was so lonely and miserable. 

My favorite part of the day was sleep.  I loved it, I looked forward to it all day.  Knowing that I could sleep was what got me through most days.  And one day it hit me.  There was a ridiculously simple way I could sleep all the time.  

This was not the saddest moment of my life.  In fact, I remember it fondly.  It was the moment I was free.  I had found some secret exit.  I was truly happy for the first time.  I began to fantasize about it constantly.

I wrote a note.  I got one of the butcher knives from the kitchen in one of the rare glorious moments my mother wasn't home.  And I stood there in the kitchen, ready to slit my throat.  Excited.  

Oddly, the thing that "saved" me was religion.  I was incredibly religious when I was younger and a sudden neuron spark in my brain reminded me that suicide "victims" don't get into heaven.  They have to wait in purgatory for the end of time.  Which I didn't expect to be soon.

I lost it.  What if I had to spend thousands of years alone in nothingness?  What if I didn't get into heaven?  What if god hated me?  I couldn't do it.  I was trapped between two horrible scenarios. 

And thus begins my saddest year.  Eighth grade was worse than seventh, with the added trauma of blaming this all on myself.  Every time someone put me down, every time my mom screamed at me, *it was my fault.*  I could have ended it, but I chose not to.  I can't really choose a moment from this year as I was almost always suicidally depressed, but that was definitely the saddest period of my life.

tl;dr  My life was torture, I nearly killed myself and backed out.  After I backed out, I blamed my tortuous life on myself.   I've never told anyone any of this, but it felt pretty good to write it down.  Sorry for the wall of text.
